items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: Dizzy Gillespie took a big band out.

ctx.x: Well it’s interesting too because those people before Parker, a lot of them, they reached a larger audience than Parker ever did. And it’s funny it’s not acknowledged, that bebop is technically demanding, and as wonderful as it was, did not have the audience that some of those before had. © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

I think it had a small audience — well I say small — I mean it certainly took off in a way I think, when you look back on it, but it was the urban areas. I mean first of all there were some big bands of course, like Billy Eckstine’s band and Dizzy Gillespie took a big band out. But they were playing charts, and sometimes people didn’t hear that thing they could dance to quite so much. But bebop essentially I think was small group things and it was musicians perhaps playing, I’m not saying for themselves, but it…
Which one is easier to whistle?
